title: Computed Properties vs Methods
description: Understand the caching behavior of computed properties and when to use each.

slides.title: Caching: The Key Difference
When to Use Which
slides.content:
| Feature | Computed Property | Method |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Caching | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Use for derived data | ✅ | ❌ (can be overkill) |
| Use for side effects | ❌ (should be pure) | ✅ |
| Use when arguments needed | ❌ (can't accept arguments directly) | ✅ |

**Guideline**:
- Use **computed** for data that depends on other reactive data and should be cached.
- Use **methods** when you need to perform side effects or need to pass arguments.

quizData.question: When should you use a method instead of a computed property?

options.text: When the value depends on reactive data
When you need to pass arguments to the function
When you need to display a value in the template

quizData.explanation: Computed properties cannot accept arguments. If you need to pass arguments (like `formatDate(date)`), use a method.
